Besan Chilla 
Savory chickpea-flour crepes with warming spices — a fast, protein-rich breakfast. 
~16–20g protein per adult · boosts to ~24g with paneer filling 
Jain Vegetarian 
Toddler-adapted 
Chickpea 
Night prep: 5 min (mix batter) 
Morning: 15 min 
Makes 6–8 chillas 
Mix all batter ingredients — under 5 min, no soaking needed; batter improves overnight 
Set aside toddler portion before adding chili; refrigerate both separately 
Batter 
Besan (chickpea flour) 
Water 
Fresh ginger, grated 
Green chili, chopped 
Coriander leaves, chopped 
Spices 
Ajwain (carom seeds) 
Cumin seeds 
Turmeric 
Red chili powder 
Coriander powder 
Hing 
Salt 
Optional paneer filling 
Paneer, crumbled 
Chaat masala 
Salt 
For cooking 
Oil or ghee 
Prepare batter (night before) 
Whisk besan (1½ cups) with water (¾ cup) gradually to avoid lumps 
Add ginger (1 tsp), ajwain (½ tsp), cumin seeds (½ tsp), turmeric (¼ tsp), coriander powder (½ tsp), hing (¼ tsp), salt (½ tsp) 
Fold in coriander leaves (2 tbsp) 
Toddler — split before refrigerating 
Remove ⅓ cup of batter before adding green chili or red chili powder 
Add a few drops of ghee — keeps her chillas softer 
Store separately 
Cook (morning) 
Stir batter well — add water (2–3 tbsp) if thickened overnight 
Add green chili (1) and red chili powder (¼ tsp) to adult batter 
If using paneer filling: mix crumbled paneer (½ cup) with chaat masala (¼ tsp) and salt; set aside 
Heat tawa on medium; grease with ghee (½ tsp) 
Pour (¼ cup) and spread quickly; cook 2 min until edges golden 
Add paneer filling (1 tbsp) in center if using; fold and press 1 min more 
Toddler cooking 
Cook on medium-low; small chillas (2 tbsp batter), serve flat 
A smear of ghee while warm adds calories 
Tip 
Ajwain aids digestion and gives the chilla its savory aroma. Besan batter thickens more than moong overnight — always loosen with water before cooking.

Hung curd (from 250g yogurt) 
Hemp seeds 
Pumpkin seeds

Walnuts, broken 
Flavor — sweet version 
Honey or jaggery powder 
Seasonal fruit 
Flavor — savory version 
Roasted cumin powder 
Black salt (kala namak) 
Cucumber, finely diced 
Coriander leaves 
To serve alongside 
Multigrain toast or makhana 
Morning assembly 
Unwrap hung curd (~1½ cups) — should be thick like labneh 
Divide into two adult bowls (~¾ cup each) 
Sweet: drizzle honey (1 tsp), add fruit (½ cup), top with hemp seeds (2 tbsp), pumpkin seeds (2 tbsp), almonds (8–10) and walnuts (4–5 halves)

Protein math 
Hung curd yields ~10–12g protein per 100g. Hemp seeds add 10g per 3 tbsp. Together with nuts you're at 22–28g with zero cooking.

Full-fat yogurt

Make batter 
Whisk besan (2 cups) with yogurt (½ cup) and water (¾ cup) — no lumps 
Add ginger (1 tsp), turmeric (½ tsp), hing (¼ tsp), lemon juice (2 tbsp), sugar (1 tsp), salt (1 tsp) 
Split batter now — remove ¾ cup into a separate dish for toddler before adding chili 
Add green chili paste (1 tsp) to adult batter only; rest both 5 min 
Toddler batch 
Her ¾ cup is already set aside — mild, chili-free 
Add Eno (½ tsp), pour into greased katori; steam 8–10 min (thinner layer) 
Steam (Instant Pot) 
Add water (1½ cups) to IP inner pot; place trivet 
Add Eno (1½ tsp) to adult batter — stir quickly until foamy; do not overmix 
Pour immediately into greased tin (~1 inch layer); place on trivet 
Steam 12–15 min with valve open — toothpick should come out clean 
Cool 5 min before cutting 
Tempering 
Heat oil (2 tbsp); add mustard seeds (1 tsp) — splutter 
Add curry leaves (10–12) and green chili (2, slit) 
Add water (3 tbsp), sugar (1 tsp), lemon juice (1 tbsp); quick boil 
Pour evenly over cut dhokla; let soak 5 min 
Garnish with coriander (2 tbsp) and coconut (2 tbsp) 
Toddler reheat 
Reheat her pieces separately — microwave (45 sec) with a splash of water 
Serve in small pieces; pair with plain yogurt or warm milk 
Key to fluffy dhokla 
Add Eno at the last second and get batter into the steamer within 60 seconds — the reaction is fast. Waiting = flat dhokla.

Add makhana (3–4 cups); dry roast, stirring constantly, 8–10 min until they feel light and crisp when pressed

Cool completely on a plate; store in an airtight jar once fully cool

Add soft fruit pieces (¼ cup) to round it out 
Tip 
Serve the yogurt and makhana in separate bowls — pouring yogurt over makes makhana go soggy fast. Dip and eat as you go.

Make dry chutney (~10 min) 
Pulse roasted peanuts (1 cup) in a dry blender — 5–6 short pulses until coarse crumble; do not over-blend into paste 
Add dry red chili (2), cumin seeds (½ tsp), hing (¼ tsp), salt (½ tsp), aamchur (1 tsp)

Morning assembly 
Heat roti (2) on tawa — 30 sec per side; smear ghee (½ tsp) while warm

Mix (1 tsp) chutney with yogurt (1 tbsp) to make a mild creamy spread 
Soft roti cut into strips or small pieces — easier for her to manage than a roll 
Add soft paneer pieces or thinly sliced cucumber inside 
Tip 
The chutney is the protein workhorse here — 2 tbsp of dry peanut chutney has ~7–8g protein. Double-layer it for more flavor and protein.

Dry roast rava and peanuts 
Heat a wide pan on medium; add rava (1 cup) — dry roast 3–4 min, stirring constantly until lightly golden and fragrant 
Remove and set aside

Finish with lemon juice (1 tsp) and coriander (2 tbsp)

Roasting rava before cooking is non-negotiable — it prevents lumpy upma. Add water slowly and stir constantly as it goes in.

Thalipeeth 
A multigrain flatbread of jowar, besan, and wheat, patted straight onto the tawa. 
~18–22g protein per adult (2 thalipeeths) — besan + jowar + wheat combined 
Jain Vegetarian 
Toddler-adapted 
Multigrain · Flatbread 
Night prep: mix dry flour blend 
Morning: 20 min 
Makes 4–5 thalipeeths (2 adults + toddler) 
Mix dry flour blend and store in a jar — lasts months, make a big batch 
Mix dough the night before with all additions; refrigerate wrapped in damp cloth 
Bhajani flour blend (large batch) 
Jowar (sorghum) flour 
Besan (chickpea flour) 
Whole wheat flour 
Rice flour 
Dough (per batch, 4–5 thalipeeths) 
Bhajani flour blend 
Fresh ginger, grated 
Green chili, very finely chopped 
Salt 
Hot water, to bind 
Spices & mix-ins 
Cumin seeds 
Hing 
Turmeric 
Coriander leaves, chopped 
Sesame seeds 
For cooking & serving 
Ghee or oil 
Plain yogurt 
White butter (loni) 
Mix dough (night before) 
Combine bhajani flour (2 cups), ginger (1 tsp), cumin seeds (½ tsp), hing (¼ tsp), turmeric (¼ tsp), sesame seeds (1 tbsp), coriander (3 tbsp), salt (¾ tsp) 
Add hot water (¾ cup) gradually; mix into a soft pliable dough — add more water as needed 
Set aside toddler portion (¼ cup dough) before adding green chili to adult dough 
Add green chili (1, finely chopped) to adult dough; knead briefly 
Wrap both portions in damp cloth; refrigerate 
Toddler dough 
Her ¼ cup portion is already chili-free — same flour blend, same spices except green chili 
Make 1–2 smaller, thinner thalipeeths for her — thinner = softer when cooked 
Cook on medium-low; add a small cube of white butter on top while warm 
Serve with a small bowl of yogurt for dipping 
Cook (morning) 
Remove dough from fridge; let sit 5 min at room temperature 
Wet your palm slightly — thalipeeth dough is patted directly onto the tawa, not rolled 
Place a ball of dough (slightly larger than a golf ball) on a greased medium-hot tawa 
Pat out gently with wet fingers into a thin round circle (~6–7 in); make 3–4 small holes in the surface with your finger 
Drizzle ghee (½ tsp) into the holes and around the edges 
Cook on medium 3–4 min until underside is golden; flip carefully 
Drizzle ghee (½ tsp) on the other side; cook 2–3 min more 
Serve hot with yogurt (alongside) and white butter (optional) 
Tip 
Wet hands are essential — thalipeeth dough is sticky and can't be rolled with a pin. Keep a small bowl of water nearby and re-wet between each one.

text:
Kadai Paneer Gravy 
A cashew-tomato kadai gravy with fresh-ground masala — no onion, no garlic, full of body. 
~12–14g protein per adult serving — from paneer 
Jain Vegetarian 
Toddler-adapted 
Paneer · Curry 
400g paneer 
6 adult servings 
~45 min 
Kadai masala — grind fresh 
Coriander seeds 
Kashmiri red chilies 
Fennel seeds (saunf) 
Green cardamoms 
Cloves 
Ceylon cinnamon 
Tomato-cashew base 
Ghee 
Fresh tomatoes 
Tomato paste 
Cashews 
Salt 
Vegetables & paneer 
Paneer, cubed 
Mixed bell peppers 
Celery, sliced 
Ghee, for tossing 
Gravy — spices & liquid 
Ghee 
Hing 
Fresh ginger paste 
Tomato paste 
Kashmiri chili powder 
Garam masala 
Salt, adjust 
Water 
Finish 
Kasuri methi 
Heavy cream, optional 
Ginger, julienned 
Fresh coriander, chopped 
Grind masala, build the base 
Add coriander seeds (3 tbsp), Kashmiri chilies (2–3, deseeded), fennel seeds (1½ tsp), cardamoms (4–5), cloves (3), and cinnamon (¼ in — hard limit, don't increase) to a spice grinder; blitz to a fine-ish powder. No need to roast — set aside. 
Heat ghee (1½ tbsp) in a deep pan on medium; add cashews (12) and toast until pale gold, 1–2 min 
Add tomatoes (400g, chopped) and salt (¼ tsp); once softened (3–4 min), stir in tomato paste (2 tbsp) 
Cover and cook on medium until completely mushy, 10–12 min 
Cool fully, then blend to a smooth paste — no water needed; set aside 
Char the vegetables & paneer 
Wipe the pan clean; heat ghee (1 tbsp) until smoking on the highest flame 
Add celery (2 stalks, sliced) and bell peppers (1½ cups, cubed); toss constantly 90 sec — charred edges, not steamed 
Add paneer (400g, cubed, patted dry); toss 60–90 sec only — do not overcook 
Set aside a small handful of paneer and capsicum separately for the toddler portion 
Transfer the rest to a plate and set aside 
Bloom hing, build the masala 
Add ghee (1 tbsp) to the pan; add hing (¼ tsp) to the cold ghee and let it bloom as the oil heats — it will foam briefly 
Add ginger paste (1½ tsp); sauté on medium 1–2 min until the raw smell fades 
Add tomato paste (1 tbsp); fry 60 sec until it darkens slightly 
Add all the kadai masala (from Step 1); sauté on low-medium 2–3 min until deeply fragrant — don't rush 
Add the base and simmer 
Add the blended tomato-cashew paste (from Step 1); sauté 3–4 min until the masala tightens and ghee separates at the sides 
Pour in water (1½–2 cups) and salt (1¼ tsp, adjust); bring to a boil, then simmer 5 min 
Toddler portion — pull before chili powder goes in 
Right now, before chili powder or garam masala go in: scoop out ½ cup of gravy — hing, ginger, and the tomato-cashew base are all fine for her 
Add the paneer and capsicum pieces set aside earlier, plus ½ cup boiled diced carrot or potato 
Thin with 2 tbsp water if needed; simmer 1 minute 
Spice and finish the gravy 
Add Kashmiri chili powder (½ tsp) and garam masala (¾ tsp) to the adult gravy; simmer 3–5 more min until it thickens and oil floats on top 
Crush kasuri methi (1½ tsp) between your palms and stir in; taste and adjust salt and garam masala 
Optional: stir in heavy cream (3 tbsp) on low heat for a silkier finish 
Add the remaining sautéed paneer (rest of the 400g), capsicum (rest of the 1½ cups) and celery (2 stalks) back into the gravy; stir gently to coat 
Turn off the heat; scatter ginger juliennes (½ inch, matchsticks) over the top 
Add fresh coriander (3 tbsp, chopped); cover and rest 2 min — the juliennes bloom in residual heat 
Rest before serving 
Transfer to a serving vessel; rest at least 15 min off heat — this is when paneer absorbs the masala flavors, don't skip 
Serve with fresh roti, paratha, or jeera rice 
Reheats well with a splash of water on the stovetop — don't microwave at high power, it toughens the paneer; keeps 3 days refrigerated 
Tip 
You'll use just under half the 170g tomato paste can — refrigerate the rest, it keeps 1–2 weeks. The ginger juliennes at the end aren't redundant with the ginger paste earlier — raw and matchstick-cut, they add a fresh, sharp bite the cooked paste doesn't have.

Stir in cream (⅓ cup) and butter (2 tbsp) 
Adjust salt to taste 
Simmer 2 more minutes on low heat, then turn off 
Cool and store for meal prep

Use the stovetop pressure cooker for the dal — it needs less water than open-pot cooking and gives the creamy, broken-down texture dal makhani needs. title: Crunchy Dumpling Lettuce Wraps
subtitle: Korean-inspired lettuce wraps with a Jain TVP filling, homemade gochujang, and crunchy dumpling strips.
protein: ~20g protein per adult serving — from TVP, plus peanuts in the chili crisp
text:
Crunchy Dumpling Lettuce Wraps 
Korean-inspired lettuce wraps with a Jain TVP filling, homemade gochujang, and crunchy dumpling strips. 
~20g protein per adult serving — from TVP, plus peanuts in the chili crisp 
Jain Vegetarian 
Toddler-adapted 
TVP · Fusion 
4 servings 
~50 min 
≈14 lettuce cups 
TVP base 
Dry TVP (granules/chunks) 
Hot water 
Reduced-sodium soy sauce 
Fresh ginger, grated 
Hing 
Sugar 
Jain gochujang (makes ⅔ cup) 
Gochugaru (Korean chili flakes) 
White miso paste 
Light brown sugar or jaggery 
Rice vinegar 
Warm water 
Salt 
Jain chili crisp (makes ½ cup) 
Neutral oil (peanut or canola) 
Fresh ginger, finely julienned 
Gochugaru or Kashmiri chili flakes 
Sesame seeds 
Roasted peanuts, crushed 
Hing 
Sugar 
Salt 
Sauce 
Reduced-sodium soy sauce 
Water 
Toasted sesame oil 
Light brown sugar 
Cornstarch 
Jain gochujang (from above) 
Filling 
Neutral oil 
Hing 
Celery, sliced thin diagonal 
Fresh ginger, grated 
Green cabbage, shredded 
Red bell pepper, julienned 
Crunchy dumpling strips 
Eggless dumpling wrappers 
Neutral oil, for frying 
White pepper 
Dried mushroom powder, optional 
Sugar 
Salt 
Assembly 
Butter lettuce 
Toasted sesame seeds 
Celery leaves or coriander 
Jain chili crisp (from above) 
Soak the TVP 
Stir together hot water (2 cups), soy sauce (1½ tbsp), grated ginger (1 tsp), hing (¼ tsp) and sugar (½ tsp) in a large bowl 
Add the dry TVP (150g) and stir well 
Cover and set aside for 15–20 minutes. It returns in Step 8 with all its liquid. 
Make the Jain gochujang 
In a small bowl, whisk gochugaru (3 tbsp — or 2 tbsp Kashmiri chili powder + 1 tbsp regular chili powder), white miso (2 tbsp), brown sugar (2 tbsp), rice vinegar (1 tbsp) and salt (¼ tsp) 
Add warm water (3 tbsp) a spoonful at a time, whisking, until it forms a thick glossy paste that falls slowly off the spoon 
Let it rest 10 minutes so the chili flakes hydrate and the raw edge softens 
Makes about ⅔ cup — you need 2 tbsp today, the rest keeps refrigerated for a month 
Make the Jain chili crisp 
Put gochugaru (2 tbsp), sesame seeds (1 tbsp), crushed peanuts (2 tbsp), hing (¼ tsp), sugar (½ tsp) and salt (½ tsp) into a heatproof bowl 
Heat neutral oil (⅓ cup) with the julienned ginger (1 tbsp) in a small pan over medium heat, 4–5 minutes, until the ginger is pale gold and the bubbling slows 
Take the pan off the heat, wait 30 seconds, then pour the oil (⅓ cup) and ginger (1 tbsp) over the bowl — it will sizzle hard for a few seconds 
Stir and cool completely. Set aside — it goes on at serving, Step 10. 
Mix the sauce, reserve the toddler's share 
Whisk soy sauce (5 tbsp), water (6 tbsp), toasted sesame oil (2 tbsp), brown sugar (2 tbsp) and cornstarch (1 tbsp) until completely smooth, no lumps 
Scoop 3 tbsp of this plain sauce into a small bowl and set it aside — that's the toddler's, and it returns in her portion right after Step 8, before the gochujang goes in 
Now stir the Jain gochujang (2 tbsp) into the sauce left in the big bowl. Set aside. 
Prep everything else 
Slice celery (2 stalks) thin on a sharp diagonal — you want long shards, not chunks 
Shred the cabbage (~4 cups), julienne the red bell pepper (1 medium), grate the ginger (2 tbsp) 
Julienne a small carrot and keep it in a separate bowl — toddler only. Microwave it with water (1 tbsp), covered, 2 minutes until just tender; drain and set aside — it returns in her portion right after Step 8. 
Stack the dumpling wrappers (14) and cut into strips about ½ cm wide 
Separate, wash and thoroughly dry the butter lettuce (2 heads) into cups — wet leaves make the filling slide out 
Crisp the dumpling strips 
Air fryer (recommended): toss the strips with oil (1 tbsp) until barely slicked. Spread in a single layer in the Ninja Crispi and run 330°F for 4–6 minutes, shaking at the 3-minute mark. Pull them while still pale gold — they darken and crisp further as they cool. 
Deep-fry alternative: heat oil (2 cups) in a heavy saucepan over high heat; fry the strips in batches, stirring gently, until golden. Lift onto a lined plate. 
Set the finished strips aside — they get seasoned next, then go on at serving, Step 10 
Toddler — pull her strips now, before seasoning 
Take a small handful of the crisped strips out and put them on her plate 
Salt them very lightly and leave them alone otherwise 
Do this before the next step — white pepper is mild but there's no reason for her to have it 
Season the adult strips 
Toss the remaining strips with white pepper (¼ tsp), mushroom powder (½ tsp), sugar (¼ tsp) and salt (¼ tsp) while still warm 
Cook the filling 
Heat neutral oil (2 tbsp) in a large sauté pan over medium-high heat 
Add hing (¼ tsp) and swirl for 10 seconds until it smells savory and nutty — don't let it brown 
Add the celery (2 stalks) and grated ginger (2 tbsp). Cook 2 minutes — the celery should stay squeaky, not go soft. 
Add the shredded cabbage (~4 cups) and red bell pepper (1 medium). Cook 5–7 minutes until the cabbage wilts and the pepper just softens. 
Add the soaked TVP (150g) from Step 1 along with all its remaining liquid. Stir through and cook 2 minutes. Stop here — nothing spicy has gone in yet. 
Toddler — pull her filling now, before the gochujang sauce 
Scoop about 1 cup of the filling and TVP out of the pan into a small saucepan 
Add the softened carrot from Step 5 
Pour in the plain reserved sauce (3 tbsp) from Step 4 
Simmer 2 minutes, stirring, until it thickens and coats everything 
Finish off the heat with ghee (½ tsp) 
Serve with her plain salted strips from earlier, and either torn butter lettuce or a small bowl of rice 
Hing and ginger are already in this and both are fine for her — the only things she's missing are the gochujang and the chili crisp; everything else is identical to the adult version, carrot included 
Finish the adult filling 
Pour the gochujang sauce from Step 4 over what's left in the big pan 
Cook 5–7 minutes, stirring, until the sauce is glossy and thick enough to sit in a lettuce leaf without running out the bottom 
Taste and adjust salt — it should be sweet-salty first, heat second 
Assemble 
Spoon the filling into the butter lettuce cups from Step 5 
Top each with the seasoned dumpling strips from Step 7, toasted sesame seeds (2 tbsp) and chopped celery leaves (¼ cup) 
Finish with Jain chili crisp (to taste) from Step 3 
Add the strips right at the table — they go soft within a couple of minutes of touching the sauce 
What changed from the original 
Onion → celery, sliced thin, plus hing bloomed in the oil. Garlic → hing. Green onion → celery leaves or coriander. Carrot → red bell pepper for adults (real carrot stays only in the toddler's portion). Bouillon cube → soy sauce + ginger + hing in the soaking water — cubes almost always carry onion or garlic powder. Gochujang and chili crisp are made from scratch here since most jarred brands, including Lao Gan Ma, list garlic. "Chicken spice" → white pepper, sugar, salt, mushroom powder. Wrappers: buy Chinese-style (flour, water, salt) — some gyoza wrappers contain egg, check the packet. 
Appliance notes 
Ninja Crispi for the strips: it runs hotter than most air fryers, 330°F is its floor and it's plenty here — start checking at 3 minutes, these go from pale to burnt in about 45 seconds. Wide sauté pan, not a wok, for the filling — you want the cabbage to wilt and lose water fast, a crowded pan steams it into mush. Small pan for the chili crisp — deep enough that ⅓ cup of oil is at least 2cm deep, or the ginger scorches before it crisps. Instant Pot isn't useful here — nothing benefits from pressure, and TVP just needs a soak. 
Recipe notes 
Celery is doing real work — slice it thin on a steep diagonal; cut into rounds it reads as "celery," cut into shards it reads as the sweet allium note the original wanted. Salt check: there's soy sauce in both the TVP soak and the sauce, so taste before adding extra salt at Step 9. The gochujang improves overnight — if you make it a day ahead, the miso rounds out and the chili loses its raw bite. No dumpling wrappers? Cut flour tortillas or spring roll pastry into strips instead — same treatment, slightly less shattery. Leftovers: filling keeps 3 days refrigerated and reheats well; store the strips and chili crisp separately at room temperature, never in the fridge. Heat level is moderate as written — halve the gochujang for a milder version, or serve it on the side and let people stir their own in.

title: Moong Dal Vada / Gâteau Piment

ingredients: Moong dal or split peas, soaked
text:
Moong Dal Vada / Gâteau Piment 
Fried lentil fritters, two ways — Indian moong dal vada or Mauritian gâteau piment. 
~10–12g protein per adult serving — from moong dal or split peas 
Jain Vegetarian 
Toddler-adapted 
Dal Vada · Fusion 
Soak: 2–12 hrs (varies) 
Cook: ~30 min 
~14 vadas + toddler 
Indian moong dal vada: soak 1 cup yellow moong dal (split, skinned) 2–3 hours 
Mauritian gâteau piment: soak 1 cup yellow split peas 8–12 hours — they need much longer 
Drain well before grinding 
Vada base 
Moong dal or split peas, soaked 
Fresh ginger, grated 
Hing 
Cumin seeds 
Coriander seeds, crushed 
Turmeric 
Salt 
Adult spicing (after toddler pull) 
Green chili, chopped 
Curry leaves (or thyme) 
Fresh cilantro, chopped 
Toddler portion 
Boiled potato, mashed 
Ghee 
Frying 
Neutral oil, for frying 
Ghee, for toddler patties 
Grind the base 
Drain the soaked dal or split peas (1 cup) well — split peas feel firmer than dal even after a long soak 
Add to a blender with ginger (1 tbsp) and a pinch of the salt 
Pulse to a coarse, thick paste — no added water; batter should hold its shape on a spoon. Split peas grind a bit coarser than moong dal — a few small flecks are normal and give gâteau piment its characteristic bite. 
Transfer to a mixing bowl 
Season the base 
Mix in hing (¼ tsp), cumin seeds (1 tsp), crushed coriander seeds (1 tsp), and turmeric (¼ tsp) 
Mix in remaining salt to taste 
This is the shared base — no chili has gone in yet 
Toddler portion — pull now 
Scoop out about ⅓ cup of the seasoned base into a separate bowl before any chili is added 
Fold in mashed potato (3 tbsp) and ghee (1 tsp) to soften the texture 
Set aside — this bowl stays out of all remaining adult steps 
Spice the adult batter 
Into the remaining base, mix in green chili (1–2), and your chosen herb — curry leaves (10 leaves) for the Indian version, or fresh thyme (1 tbsp) for Mauritian — plus cilantro (3 tbsp) 
Mix evenly — this is now the adult batter only 
Shape and fry the adult batch 
Heat oil (as needed) in a kadai or heavy pot over medium-high heat 
Wet hands, shape adult batter into small flat patties (~2 tbsp each) — for gâteau piment, shape slightly thicker in the center than a typical vada 
Fry in batches until deep golden and firm — 3–4 minutes per side for moong dal, 4–5 minutes for split peas, which take a little longer to cook through 
Drain on a rack or paper towel 
Cook the toddler patties 
Heat ghee (1 tbsp) in a small nonstick pan over medium-low heat 
Shape the toddler batter into 3–4 small, thin patties (thinner than the adult ones, for a soft bite) 
Pan-sear 2–3 minutes per side until set through and lightly golden — no raw batter should remain 
Cool and cut into soft strips before serving to reduce choking risk 
About this recipe 
These are culinary cousins — both trace back to Indian indentured-labor cooking traditions, but diverged: Indian moong dal vada uses skinned split mung bean and curry leaves; Mauritian gâteau piment traditionally uses yellow split peas and thyme (often chives too, swapped here for cilantro to stay onion/garlic-free for Jain). Toor dal isn't offered as a third option — it's too soft and crumbly to hold together fried this way; it's better suited to dal fry or sambar. Texture check: batter should hold together without added water — too wet, add a spoon of chickpea flour; too dry, add a few drops of water at a time. 
Appliance & storage 
Stovetop kadai works best for the adult batch either way. For a lighter version in the Ninja Crispi, brush patties with oil and air-fry at 350°F for 8–10 minutes, flipping halfway — add 2–3 minutes for the split-pea version, and check a bit early since the Crispi runs hot. Toddler patties stay stovetop pan-seared, not air-fried; their thin shape dries out fast in the Crispi. Leftover vadas keep 3 days refrigerated and re-crisp nicely in a dry pan, or the Crispi at 330°F for 3–4 minutes.

title: Dry Peanut Chutney
subtitle: A ground peanut condiment with chana dal and sesame — mild enough for the whole family.
protein: ~3g protein per 2 tbsp serving — from peanuts, chana dal & sesame
text:
Dry Peanut Chutney 
A ground peanut condiment with chana dal and sesame — mild enough for the whole family. 
~3g protein per 2 tbsp serving — from peanuts, chana dal & sesame 
Jain Vegetarian 
Toddler-adapted 
Condiment · Bulk Batch 
Prep: 10 min 
Cook: 20 min 
Yields ~5 cups (stores 3–4 wks) 
To roast separately 
Raw peanuts, skin-on 
White sesame seeds 
Tempered spice base 
Kashmiri red chilies 
Cumin seeds 
Dry coconut, grated 
Tamarind, seedless 
Curry leaves 
Neutral oil, tempering 
Added at grinding 
Roasted chana dal (dalia) 
Salt 
Hing 
Roast peanuts (Ninja Crispi) 
Spread peanuts (3 cups) in the Crispi basket in a single layer — you'll likely need 2 batches of 1½ cups each to avoid steaming 
Set to 330°F, 6 min — this is the Crispi's lowest usable setting, it won't run cooler 
Shake the basket at the 3-minute mark 
Check at 5 min: peanuts should be fragrant, skins loosening and crackled; since 330°F runs hot for this, add only 1 min at a time from here 
Spread on a plate and cool completely, at least 15 min — they crisp further as they cool 
Rub between palms to loosen skins; sieve or blow away (a little remaining skin is fine) 
Roast sesame (cooktop) 
In a dry pan over low flame, add sesame seeds (3 tbsp) 
Stir constantly 60–90 sec — they will pop and jump; keep a lid nearby 
Remove the moment they turn lightly golden and smell toasty — they burn in seconds if you walk away 
Cool completely on a separate plate; keep aside for grinding 
Temper the spices 
Heat oil (2 tsp) in a small pan over medium-low 
Add curry leaves (2 sprigs); fry 20–30 sec until crisp; remove and set aside 
In the same pan on low, add Kashmiri chilies (12) and cumin seeds (1 tbsp); roast, stirring, 60–90 sec until cumin is golden — do not blacken 
Add coconut (4 tbsp, or 2½ tbsp if thawed frozen) and tamarind (1½ tsp); toss 30 sec until coconut is lightly golden 
Return the curry leaves (2 sprigs) to the pan; transfer everything to a plate and cool completely 
Grind — spice base first, then peanuts 
Add the cooled chili-cumin-coconut-tamarind-curry leaf mixture to a grinder 
Add chana dal (½ cup) and the toasted sesame (3 tbsp) — these must be ground fine now, not pulsed later with the peanuts 
Add hing (¾ tsp) and salt (2 tsp); grind to a fine powder, 25–35 sec 
Add the roasted, cooled peanuts (3 cups) 
Pulse only — 3–4 short bursts of 2–3 sec each — until coarse and sandy, not paste 
Taste and adjust salt 
Toddler notes 
This whole batch is already toddler-mild — the 12 Kashmiri chilies give color, not real heat 
For more adult heat, add chili flakes separately at serving time rather than into the batch 
Serve her portion mixed with a few drops of ghee, or stirred into warm dal-rice for easier eating 
Great sprinkled on her soft roti with ghee, or mixed into yogurt rice 
Cool, store, label 
Spread the finished chutney on a wide plate; rest uncovered 20 min to drive off residual moisture 
Transfer to a clean, dry, airtight glass jar 
Store at room temperature 3–4 weeks, or refrigerate to extend to 6–8 weeks — if frozen coconut was used, drop to 2–3 weeks and refrigerate after the first week 
Always use a dry spoon — a single drop of moisture shortens shelf life fast 
Label the jar with the date made 
Tip 
Grind the spice base to a fine powder before the peanuts ever go in, then only pulse the peanuts in short bursts — their oil releases fast and a few seconds too long turns the whole batch into peanut butter. If using frozen coconut, dry it on the stovetop first, not in the Crispi (it browns the dry bits before the wet ones catch up). Great over hot rice with ghee, mixed into yogurt rice, or stuffed into a roti roll.

title: Maggi Masala Powder

protein: One batch seasons ~16–18 dishes — keeps 3–4 months at room temp
text:
Maggi Masala Powder 
A unified spice blend for Maggi noodles and more — tuned so overlapping spices don't double up. 
One batch seasons ~16–18 dishes — keeps 3–4 months at room temp 
Jain Vegetarian 
Toddler-adapted 
Spice Blend 
Yield: ~8 oz jar 
Prep: 5 min 
~16–18 uses 
Clean base — no overlap 
Coriander powder 
Roasted jeera (cumin) powder 
Red chili powder 
Turmeric (haldi) 
Blended masalas 
Chaat masala 
Garam masala 
Reduced standalones 
Dry ginger powder (soonth) 
Aamchur (mango powder) 
Black pepper powder 
Salt 
Body & balance 
Corn flour (cornstarch) 
Sugar 
Hing 
Measure everything into one bowl 
Use a large dry bowl — everything goes in together 
Measure coriander powder (¾ cup) first — it's your visual anchor, everything else is much smaller relative to it 
Add roasted jeera (3 tsp), chili powder (2 tbsp), turmeric (1 tbsp) 
Add chaat masala (2 tbsp) and garam masala (1½ tbsp) 
Add ginger powder (¾ tsp), aamchur (1½ tsp), black pepper (¾ tsp), salt (1½ tsp) 
Add corn flour (1½ tbsp), sugar (1½ tsp), hing (½ tsp) 
Mix until uniform 
Whisk or stir with a dry spoon for at least 1 minute 
No streaks of turmeric yellow or chili red should be visible when done 
Final color should be a warm reddish-brown — not orange, not dark brown 
Dry taste test 
Take a tiny pinch — rub between fingers and taste dry before jarring 
You should get: sour hit first, then warmth, then mild heat, savory salt undertone 
If something feels off, see the taste tuning notes below before transferring to jar 
Transfer to jar 
Use a completely dry 8 oz glass jar with a tight-sealing lid 
Funnel or spoon the blend in — tap to settle, don't pack it down 
Label with: Maggi Masala · date made · v1 — track adjustments batch to batch 
Never close the lid if anything is warm — moisture causes clumping 
Toddler note 
Use ¼ tsp maximum per toddler serving — chaat masala and chili make this moderately spiced 
For her Maggi bowl: cook noodles plain, season her portion separately with ¼ tsp 
Stir in small cubed boiled carrot or potato for added nutrition and bulk 
Why it's built this way 
Chaat masala and garam masala both carry pepper, cumin, ginger, and salt, so the standalone amounts of those four are dialed back to avoid doubling up. Aamchur replaces citric acid for a more natural sour note. Hing is added on top for Jain depth. 
How to use this jar 
Maggi noodles: 1–1½ tsp per adult serving. Stir-fried vegetables or sabji: 1 tsp per 2 servings. Paneer marinade: 1½ tsp per 200g. Air-fryer paneer or peanuts: ¾–1 tsp per batch. Chaat sprinkle or raita seasoning: ½ tsp to taste. 
Storage 
Keep in a cool, dark spot away from the stove. Shelf life 3–4 months at room temperature, up to 6 months refrigerated in a sealed bag. Clumping means moisture got in — break it up and use within 2 weeks. Always scoop with a dry spoon, and label the jar with the date and "v1" to track adjustments. 
Taste tuning (after first cooked use) 
Too spicy: stir in a little more coriander powder to dilute this jar; reduce chili next batch. Not sour enough: add more aamchur — it adds tang without extra salt. Tastes flat: add a touch more hing, the umami anchor here. Bitter aftertaste: usually the turmeric or over-toasted jeera — make sure roasted jeera is store-bought, not home-toasted past golden. Too salty: your chaat masala brand is likely running salty — use less per serving rather than fixing the jar.

text:
Sambar Powder 
A toasted spice and lentil powder — the base for sambar, rasam, and general souring or spicing. 
Makes ~1 cup — enough for many batches of sambar or rasam, keeps 3 months 
Jain Vegetarian 
Toddler-adapted 
Sambar · Spice Blend 
Prep: 5 min 
Roast: 10 min 
Yield: ~1 cup 
Dals & chilies 
Chana dal (bengal gram) 
Urad dal, skinned (black gram) 
Toor dal (split pigeon peas) 
Dried red chilies 
Seeds 
Coriander seeds 
Methi seeds (fenugreek) 
Cumin seeds 
Black peppercorns, optional 
Aromatics & finish 
Curry leaves, optional 
Hing 
Turmeric powder 
Dry roast in stages 
Heat a heavy pan on low flame — low heat the whole way through is what brings out the aroma, don't rush this 
Add chana dal (1½ tbsp), urad dal (1½ tbsp), toor dal (1 tbsp), and dried red chilies (8–12); dry roast, stirring often, until the dals turn golden and the chilies darken slightly and smell toasty 
Add coriander seeds (¼ cup) and methi seeds (¾ tsp); roast until the coriander turns crunchy and lightly golden, and the methi turns a shade darker and smells nutty 
Once fragrant, add curry leaves (2 sprigs) if using; roast until they turn crisp and shatter easily 
Add cumin seeds (2 tsp) and peppercorns (1 tsp) if using; roast until the cumin turns crunchy and fragrant, then turn off the flame 
With the flame off, stir in turmeric (¼ tsp) and hing (⅛ tsp) — residual heat blooms them without scorching 
Transfer everything to a wide plate and spread out to cool completely, at least 20–30 minutes 
Grind and store 
Once fully cooled, transfer everything to a blender or spice grinder jar 
Grind to a fine, even powder 
Let the ground powder cool completely — grinding generates heat, and trapping that warmth in a sealed jar invites moisture 
Store in an airtight glass or steel jar at room temperature; keeps well for about 3 months 
Toddler note 
This is a pantry ingredient, not a dish on its own, so there's no separate toddler portion here 
It's spicy — dried whole chilies and pepper — so whenever you use it later in a sambar, rasam, or anything else, pull her portion before this powder goes in, same as with any other chili step 
Equipment 
Stovetop pan for roasting, then a dry spice or coffee grinder for the final powder — no air fryer or pressure cooker needed here.

Spiced Chaas 
Mint · Roasted cumin · 5 min · 2 adults + toddler 
~8g protein per batch (~3g per 1-cup glass) 
Jain Vegetarian 
Toddler-adapted 
Yogurt 
Prep: 5 min 
Makes ~3 cups 
2 adults + toddler 
Base 
Plain yogurt (curd) 
Chilled water 
Roasted cumin powder 
Black salt (kala namak) 
Regular salt 
Aromatics 
Mint leaves 
Fresh coriander 
Fresh ginger 
Green chili, minced 
Adult finish (optional) 
Ghee 
Hing (asafoetida) 
Curry leaves 
Black pepper, ground 
Chaat masala 
Blend aromatics 
Add mint (10–12 leaves), coriander (small handful) and ginger (½ inch) to a blender 
Add yogurt (¼ cup) 
Blend until completely smooth 
Mix chaas 
Add remaining yogurt (¾ cup) and chilled water (2 cups) 
Add roasted cumin powder (½ tsp), black salt (½ tsp) and salt (to taste) 
Blend or whisk until light and frothy 
Toddler — pour now, before chili and pepper 
Pour her glass (½ cup) from the chaas 
Optional: stir in a tiny pinch of hing (1 pinch) and serve chilled 
Adult spicing 
Stir green chili (½, minced) and black pepper (1 pinch) into the remaining chaas 
Heat ghee (½ tsp) in a small pan on low 
Add hing (1 pinch) and curry leaves (5–6); sizzle 10 seconds 
Pour the tempering over the chaas; add chaat masala (¼ tsp) 
Chill 15 minutes or serve over ice 
Tip 
Chaas separates as it sits — whisk again just before pouring.
